title.en: AI Safety: From Tay to ASL-3
title.zhHans: AI 安全：从翻车聊天机器人到前沿安全框架

searchTitle.en: AI Safety: Incidents, Safeguards and Legal Scrutiny, 2016–2026
searchTitle.zhHans: AI 安全：2016—2026 年的事故、防护与法律审查

searchSummary.en: From Tay and staged GPT-2 release to ASL-3, deepfake investigations and 2026 consumer-protection lawsuits: different ways AI safety concerns entered product decisions and public oversight.
searchSummary.zhHans: 从 Tay、GPT-2 分阶段发布到 ASL-3、深度伪造调查与 2026 年消费者保护诉讼：AI 安全问题如何进入产品决策和公共审查。

subtitle.en: Incidents, voluntary safeguards and distinct forms of public scrutiny
subtitle.zhHans: 事故、自愿防护与不同形式的公共审查

abstract.en: Tay’s withdrawal in 2016 and the staged release of GPT-2 in 2019 illustrate early responses to different model risks. Later disputes over voice, copyright and product safety, alongside laboratory safeguards and 2026 court filings, involved different harms and authorities. This Arc asks what these responses can establish—and what remains an allegation, a voluntary commitment or an unresolved legal question. A filing is not a ruling, and restrictions on access are not proof that risks have been resolved.
abstract.zhHans: 2016 年 Tay 下线和 2019 年 GPT-2 分阶段发布，展示了对不同模型风险的早期回应。随后围绕声音、版权和产品安全的争议，以及实验室防护措施和 2026 年的诉讼，涉及不同的损害与权力主体。本专题追问：这些回应能说明什么，哪些仍是指控、自愿承诺或未决的法律问题。起诉不等于判决，限制访问也不等于风险已经消除。

narrative.en: Microsoft took Tay offline in 2016 after it posted abusive content during user interactions. Three years later, OpenAI initially withheld GPT-2’s full model, citing concerns about misuse, and released versions in stages. The two episodes are not a controlled comparison: one concerns harmful outputs from a deployed chatbot; the other concerns a lab’s release decision for a language model. Together, they offer an early view of two responses—withdraw access after observed problems and restrict access ahead of anticipated misuse. Neither event by itself shows that either response became an industry standard or resolved the risks it addressed.
narrative.zhHans: 2016 年，Tay 在与用户互动中发布冒犯性内容后，微软将其下线。三年后，OpenAI 以担忧模型遭滥用为由，起初没有发布 GPT-2 完整版本，而是分阶段开放。两件事并非可直接比较的实验：前者涉及已部署聊天机器人的有害输出，后者涉及实验室对语言模型的发布决定。它们展示了两种早期回应：问题出现后撤回访问，以及在预期风险前限制访问。单凭任何一件事，都不能证明相应做法后来成为行业标准或解决了所针对的风险。

keyInsight.en: A withdrawal after harmful output and a staged release before anticipated misuse are different safety responses; neither establishes a universal playbook.
keyInsight.zhHans: 有害输出后的下线与预期滥用前的分阶段发布，是两种不同的安全回应；都不能单独构成通用方案。

title.en: Consent and Copyright Reach the Courts
title.zhHans: 同意与版权进入法律争议

narrative.en: In 2024, Scarlett Johansson publicly objected to the resemblance between her voice and the ChatGPT voice “Sky”; OpenAI disputed that it was an imitation and paused the voice. The dispute concerned consent and likeness, not a judicial finding that OpenAI had copied her. Music companies also filed copyright complaints against Suno and Udio, alleging unauthorized use of recorded music for AI training. Whether particular uses are lawful must be assessed through the cases, not assumed from the filings. These episodes broaden this Arc beyond technical model behaviour: people creating or represented in AI products contested the terms under which their work or identity could be used. Voice consent and copyright are distinct legal questions, not interchangeable measures of model safety.
narrative.zhHans: 2024 年，Scarlett Johansson 公开反对 ChatGPT 的“Sky”语音与自己声音相似；OpenAI 否认该语音是模仿，并暂停使用。争议涉及同意与肖像声音权益，而不是法院已经认定 OpenAI 复制了她的声音。音乐公司也对 Suno 和 Udio 提起版权诉讼，指控其训练 AI 时未经许可使用录音。具体使用是否合法，须由案件审理判断，不能从起诉推定。这些事件让本专题不限于模型的技术行为：创作者及被 AI 产品呈现的人，开始质疑其作品或身份被使用的条件。语音同意和版权是不同的法律问题，不能混作模型安全性的同一种衡量。

keyInsight.en: Legal challenges to voice use and music training raise different questions about consent and rights; allegations remain allegations.
keyInsight.zhHans: 针对声音使用与音乐训练的法律争议，涉及不同的同意和权利问题；诉讼指控仍只是指控。

title.zhHans: 举报争议与实验室防护

narrative.en: Former OpenAI researcher Suchir Balaji had raised concerns about copyrighted training data. A San Francisco medical examiner ruled his death a suicide in 2025. His death is not evidence that an AI system caused it, nor does temporal proximity establish that it caused later legislation. Separately, Anthropic said it had activated ASL-3 safeguards for some advanced models under its Responsible Scaling Policy. An internal safeguard framework describes a company practice; it is not an independent measurement that all model risks have been contained. Placing these events together highlights two distinct accountability questions: how concerns raised by people inside the industry are heard, and how labs specify and test safeguards. No causal link between the two events is asserted.
narrative.zhHans: 前 OpenAI 研究员 Suchir Balaji 曾质疑受版权保护的训练数据使用方式。旧金山法医于 2025 年裁定他的死因为自杀。他的死亡不能作为 AI 系统致死的证据；时间相近也不能证明它促成了后来的立法。另一方面，Anthropic 称已依据其《负责任扩展政策》对部分先进模型启用 ASL-3 防护。企业内部防护框架说明了公司做法，并非所有模型风险都已受控的独立测量。将两件事并置，是为了讨论不同的问责问题：行业内部提出的担忧如何被倾听，以及实验室如何制定和检验防护。这里不主张两件事之间存在因果关系。

keyInsight.en: A person’s death must not be used as a causal shortcut for later policy; published lab safeguards likewise need outcome evidence to assess their effectiveness.
keyInsight.zhHans: 不能用个人死亡为后续政策建立未经证实的因果关系；实验室公布防护措施后，其成效也仍需结果证据检验。

narrative.en: The 2026 events in this chapter show several different forms of scrutiny, not a single completed crackdown. In January, Grok was used to create nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes; Indonesia and Malaysia temporarily blocked access, and the UK regulator Ofcom opened an investigation. In March, a Claude Code source-map packaging mistake exposed source code, raising a different set of operational and supply-chain security concerns. In June, Florida sued OpenAI and Sam Altman over alleged consumer-safety failures. The US Commerce Department separately issued a company-specific directive restricting access to Anthropic’s Fable 5 and Mythos 5, which Anthropic suspended for its users; the restrictions were lifted on June 30. On October 14, attorneys general in eight more states filed coordinated consumer-protection complaints alleging that OpenAI misrepresented ChatGPT’s safety. Those complaints are not judgments, injunctions, or findings of liability. Together these actions show safety and access questions reaching courts and public authorities, while their legal outcomes and real-world remedies remain unsettled.
narrative.zhHans: 本章的 2026 年事件呈现了几种不同形式的审查，而不是一场已经完成的全面整顿。1 月，Grok 被用于制作未经同意的性化深度伪造；印度尼西亚和马来西亚暂时封锁访问，英国监管机构 Ofcom 展开调查。3 月，Claude Code 的源映射打包失误暴露了源码，引出另一类运营与供应链安全问题。6 月，佛罗里达州就涉嫌侵害消费者安全的问题起诉 OpenAI 和 Sam Altman。美国商务部另行发出针对 Anthropic 的指令，限制 Fable 5 和 Mythos 5 的访问，Anthropic 因而对用户暂停服务；相关限制于 6 月 30 日解除。10 月 14 日，另外八州总检察长协调提起消费者保护诉讼，指控 OpenAI 对 ChatGPT 安全性作出误导性表述。这些诉状不是判决、禁令或责任认定。这些行动表明，安全和访问问题正进入法院与公共机构的议程，但法律结果和实际补救仍未确定。

keyInsight.en: The 2026 access restrictions, investigations and consumer-protection filings concern different authorities and harms; their outcomes cannot be inferred from the initial actions.
keyInsight.zhHans: 2026 年的访问限制、调查和消费者保护诉讼，涉及不同权力主体和损害类型；不能从启动行动推断最终结果。

conclusion.en: These episodes do not describe a single industry-wide failure or a completed regulatory settlement. Tay’s removal, GPT-2’s staged release and Anthropic’s ASL-3 approach are different responses to different risks; litigation over consent, copyright and alleged product harms raises additional questions. The Grok investigation and state complaints show public authorities taking specific steps, but investigations and complaints do not establish liability. Export controls on model access raise a national-security question distinct from whether a product is safe for users. Which safeguards reduce harm, for whom, and at what cost remains open to evidence rather than a verdict supplied by this chronology.
conclusion.zhHans: 这些事件既不能概括为全行业同一种失败，也不意味着监管争议已经尘埃落定。Tay 下线、GPT-2 分阶段发布和 Anthropic 的 ASL-3 做法，针对的是不同风险；关于同意、版权和涉嫌产品损害的诉讼又提出了其他问题。Grok 调查和州级诉讼体现了公共机构的具体行动，但调查和诉状不等于责任认定。限制模型访问的出口措施涉及国家安全问题，与产品对用户是否安全并不相同。哪些防护能够减少损害、惠及谁、代价如何，仍须由后续证据回答，而非由这条时间线代为下结论。
